chunk_findings.detail: This is the earlier “does not derive the merge’s first-parent range” defect, moved to the new helper: `_merged_range_env` only maps an already supplied `changed_from` and returns `{}` when it is empty. If the after-merge check is invoked without `changed_from` (the reported symptom is that no `PRE_COMMIT_FROM_REF` is exported) while the enclosing run already knows the merge `base`, the function still exports no range and `gitleaks-pushed.sh` again scans `origin/main..HEAD`. Even when `changed_from` is a moving ref such as `main`, it is resolved in `repo` before the suite-slot wait; if `main` advances from `A` to `B` while queued, `_run_under_slot` merges onto `B` to avoid a stale tree, but the hook receives `PRE_COMMIT_FROM_REF=A` and scans `A..HEAD`, including the `A..B` commits that were not part of this merge. The range should be derived/re-resolved from the actual merged tree’s first parent, and `PRE_COMMIT_TO_REF` should be the resolved merge commit rather than a late-bound `HEAD`.

chunk_findings.detail: The added regression test does not exercise the reported failure path. Both tests call `CI.run(..., changed_from=before)` (lines 51 and 69), so they only test the case where the caller already supplies the range. A test that always passes `changed_from` will pass even if the fix only forwards an explicitly supplied range and still does not derive/export the merge's first-parent range for the after-merge hook. Add a test that invokes the after-merge check exactly as the post-merge hook does (no `changed_from`) and asserts the hook sees the merge range, or directly test the range-derivation helper for a merge commit.

chunk_findings.detail: The `env_extra` threading stops at `_execute`: the diff adds `env_extra=None` to its signature/docstring, but no shown body line reads or forwards `env_extra` to the stages or `CommandRunner`. Thus, for a post-merge run with a known `changed_from`, `_merged_range_env` produces `PRE_COMMIT_FROM_REF`/`PRE_COMMIT_TO_REF`, `_run_under_slot`/`_run_locked` pass them into `_execute`, and `_execute` still runs the command without those variables. The child `pre-commit`/`gitleaks-pushed.sh` therefore falls back to `origin/main..HEAD` as before. This is the earlier `_execute` finding; the signature-only change does not answer it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/runner.py:_execute

chunk_findings.detail: The new `env_extra` is threaded all the way to `_execute`, but the diff does not change `_execute`'s body to actually pass it to the command execution path. Given a post-merge run where `changed_from` is a known base, `_merged_range_env` returns `{"PRE_COMMIT_FROM_REF": <sha>, "PRE_COMMIT_TO_REF": "HEAD"}`, `_run_locked`/`_run_under_slot` forward it via `**_extra(env_extra)`, and `_execute` accepts it; because the unchanged `_execute` body never adds `env_extra` to the `CommandRunner`/`_run_stages` environment, the hook still sees no `PRE_COMMIT_FROM_REF` and can fall back to `origin/main..HEAD`. The fix therefore silently drops the exported range at the last hop.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/runner.py:_execute

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression hook only checks that `PRE_COMMIT_TO_REF` is non-empty (`test -n "$PRE_COMMIT_TO_REF"`), and the tests do not clear inherited `PRE_COMMIT_*` variables before running. If `CI.run`/`check_after_merge` exports the correct `PRE_COMMIT_FROM_REF` but exports the wrong end of the range—e.g. `PRE_COMMIT_TO_REF=HEAD`, `origin/main`, or a stale value inherited from the pytest process—these tests still pass. That does not demonstrate that the merged range’s `TO_REF` is exported, only that some non-empty value is present.
